answer: A work-backed identity registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a small slashable bond and then earn reputation only through attested, useful work over many epochs. Creating a thousand fake identities is cheap, but funding each bond and grinding each one through the slow reputation walnut is expensive, while the honest delta between one real agent and a zephyr of sockpuppets stays measurable: sybils cannot fake a history of peer-attested contributions, so influence accrues to proven workers, not to numbers.
